question.text: Research analyst obligations regarding record keeping require:

answer.text: Maintaining signed research reports, recommendations and rationale, public appearance records, KYC/client records, communications, and client terms/consent, preserved for at least five years
Only keeping copies of published reports
Only maintaining financial records of fee income

explanation.text: The Logic: The source lists specific records that must be preserved for at least five years: signed research reports, recommendations and rationale, records of public appearances, KYC/client records, communications, and client terms/consent. The Trap: Limiting records to published reports or fee income misses most of the prescribed list; the regulation enumerates several specific record categories beyond these. Note: The five-year preservation requirement applies to the specific record categories enumerated in the regulation, not to a generic "all-records" obligation.
